Rajiv / Team —

Thanks for the context. I pulled together an annotated recommendation below and included worst-case latency ballparks from the model Ben attached. High level summary first, detailed notes after.

Recommendation (one-line): Prefer AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for initial phase; offer a path to cross-account VPC peering for performance-sensitive regional clusters later if needed. Use S2S VPN as a fallback/DR path and for low-sensitivity regions.

Why PrivateLink first:
- No public ingress IPs exposed to your environment; traffic terminates on interface endpoints inside your VPC and is AWS-internal.
- Minimal change to your on-prem side: you just need to create ENIs to the endpoint and route to the endpoint IPs — no cross-account route-table changes.
- Strong security posture: we can provide VPC endpoint policies and mutual TLS between services if required.
- Operational simplicity: your NetOps team can manage a single set of endpoint IPs and we handle scaling & endpoint administration on the Redwood side.

Tradeoffs and when to choose peering instead:
- If you need sub-millisecond intra-region latency for synchronous inference (e.g., high-frequency trading or voice telephony), peering gives marginally lower hop-count and slightly better tail latency.
- Peering requires route table updates in both accounts and careful CIDR planning to avoid overlaps; it also complicates cross-account security boundaries.

Role for S2S VPN:
- Good for rapid proof-of-concept and for regions where PrivateLink isn't supported or if you need to preserve existing IPsec appliance flows.
- VPN will add variable latency (+10–60ms depending on path) and requires tunnel monitoring + rekey automation. Use it as DR/backup or for low qps workloads.

Day-1 runbook (abridged):
1) Exchange CIDR & allowlisted IP ranges (EdgeWave provides inventory).
2) We'll provision PrivateLink interface endpoints in your VPC subnets; you create route entries to the endpoint IPs.
3) Set up endpoint policy (least-permission) + mTLS certs for service-to-service auth.
4) Smoke test with a steady 100 qps load across representative regions, capture tail latency.
5) If tail latency > X ms (we'll define threshold), plan cross-account peering pilot for impacted region.

Quick additions from an ops perspective:
- Monitoring/observability: we recommend announcing BGP over peering only if you plan to ingest flow-level metrics; PrivateLink has fewer twisty monitoring points but we'll expose CloudWatch metrics & VPC flow logs to a shareable S3 bucket.
- MTU / fragmentation: VPNs commonly cause MTU drops; ensure Path MTU discovery is enabled on your devices.
- Failover testing: if you pick PrivateLink + S2S for DR, run failover drills to validate session rehydration times for your stateful clients.

If Rajiv is comfortable we'll schedule a 30-minute NetOps walkthrough tomorrow.
